chunks: And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said:
Woe to the merchants of my Ummah because of “No, by Allah” and “Yes, by Allah,” and woe to the craftsmen of my Ummah because of today and tomorrow.

key_terms.بَلَى وَ ٱللَّهِ: the expression 'Yes, by Allah,' referring to frequent oath-taking
key_terms.لَا وَ ٱللَّهِ: the expression 'No, by Allah,' referring to frequent oath-taking
key_terms.لِتُجَّارِ: for merchants and traders engaged in commerce
key_terms.وَيْلٌ: a warning of woe and severe blame
key_terms.ٱلْيَوْمِ وَ غَدٍ: today and tomorrow, meaning preoccupation with immediate and future worldly concerns

ai.seo_question: What did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله say about merchants swearing oaths and workers worrying about today and tomorrow?
ai.summary: This hadith warns merchants against excessive swearing in trade and cautions craftsmen and workers against anxious worldly preoccupation with immediate gain and future provision. It teaches ethical restraint, truthful conduct, and reliance upon Allah while earning a livelihood.
